description: Table 3 is a plain rendered data table (no micrograph, spectrum, plot or schematic content) headed "Tensile properties of HRQ and annealed specimen". It has five columns — Sample Id, Yield Strength (MPa), Ultimate tensile strength (MPa), Total elongation (%), and PSE (GPa%) — and six data rows, each quoting mean ± scatter. The rows are: Hot Rolled, 486±6 MPa / 674±20 MPa / 1.5±0.5 % / 1.01 GPa%; IA750_5 Min, 460±8 / 605±7 / 4.15±.80 / 2.5; IA750_30 Min, 450±10 / 615±10 / 7±1 / 4.3; IA750_60 Min, 465±10 / 658.45±6 / 12±0.95 / 7.9; IA750_120 Min, 433±4.5 / 571±7 / 5±0.4 / 2.8; and IA750_180 Min, 427±6.5 / 570±6 / 5.5±0.5 / 3.1. All rows are fully legible. The table quantifies the room-temperature tensile response of the hot-rolled-and-quenched (HRQ) steel and of specimens intercritically annealed at 750 °C for 5, 30, 60, 120 and 180 min: strength is highest for Hot Rolled while total elongation and the product of strength and elongation (PSE) peak at IA750_60 Min (12 % elongation, 7.9 GPa%), then fall sharply at 120 and 180 min — the tabulated evidence for an optimum 60-minute annealing window.

observations.observation: The table lists six sample conditions: Hot Rolled, IA750_5 Min, IA750_30 Min, IA750_60 Min, IA750_120 Min and IA750_180 Min.
The measured columns are Yield Strength (MPa), Ultimate tensile strength (MPa), Total elongation (%) and PSE (GPa%).
Hot Rolled shows the highest yield strength (486±6 MPa) and highest ultimate tensile strength (674±20 MPa) together with the lowest total elongation (1.5±0.5 %) and the lowest PSE (1.01 GPa%).
IA750_60 Min records the maximum total elongation (12±0.95 %) and the maximum PSE (7.9 GPa%) of all six rows.
Yield strength decreases monotonically relative to Hot Rolled for all annealed specimens, reaching the lowest value, 427±6.5 MPa, for IA750_180 Min.
Total elongation is non-monotonic in annealing time: it rises from 4.15±.80 % (5 Min) to 7±1 % (30 Min) and 12±0.95 % (60 Min), then drops to 5±0.4 % (120 Min) and 5.5±0.5 % (180 Min).
PSE follows the same non-monotonic trend as elongation, peaking at 7.9 GPa% for IA750_60 Min and falling to 2.8 and 3.1 GPa% at 120 and 180 Min.
The caption states that PSE is the product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation.
The caption defines the table as tensile properties of HRQ and annealed specimens, i.e. the hot-rolled-and-quenched state plus intercritical annealing at 750 °C.

The citing text states that IA750_60 Min shows UTS of 658.45±6 MPa with maximum TE of 12±0.95 %, attributed to optimum stability of reverted austenite enhancing the TRIP effect during tensile loading.
The citing text states that the HRQ sample's high strength is mainly due to hard martensite together with retained austenite and δ-ferrite in the microstructure.
The table is presented as the tabulated counterpart of the engineering stress-strain curves in Fig. 6(A1), according to the citing text.
